newsitem.title: GERMANY: Shareholders vent anger at Hoechst share plunge.
newsitem.headline: Shareholders vent anger at Hoechst share plunge.

text.p: Shareholders at German drugs and chemicals giant Hoechst AG sharply criticised management's communications policies Tuesday, blaming them for a 22 percent drop in the company's stock price this year.

Venting their anger after watching Hoechst shares plunge as markets punished the group for failing to deliver promised strong results, shareholders said the board had gambled away trust in the 134 year-old company.

"A pledge to improve shareholder value is worth nothing if shareholders are not informed in a timely fashion," Jella Benner-Heinacher, a spokeswoman for shareholder group Deutsche Schutzvereinigung fuer Wertpapierbesitz, told the firm's annual meeting.
While Hoechst shares have slowly crawled higher again, they had plummeted from an all-time high of 80.80 marks ($46.77) on March 11 to a low of 62.80 marks ($36.35) April 3.

Announcements of a lower than expected 1996 operating profit, a fourth-quarter loss and the board's decision to shelve plans to take drugs unit Hoechst Marion Roussel public combined to trigger the fall.

Many analysts downgraded recommendations and earnings per share estimates after the slew of negative news, complaining about the company's failure to issue a profit warning about the fourth-quarter loss.
